"Lasciamo lavorare i tavoli, ma io sono fiduciosa che lavoreremo per trovare una sintesi alta su tutti i temi e che presto riusciremo insieme a interpretare una sfida elettorale fondamentale non solo per il futuro del Paese ma anche per il futuro dell'Europa", dice la segretaria dem.

articles.title: Borse di studio sospese agli studenti indagati, polemiche sull'emendamento Delmastro
articles.summary: AGI - " Revoca dei benefici nell'ambito del diritto allo studio ". È il titolo dell'emendamento presentato dal deputato di Fratelli d'Italia Andrea Delmastro al decreto scuola. Una proposta che innesca la reazione delle opposizioni: "Impunità per gli amici, repressione per studenti e lavoratori che protestano", è il commento di Giuseppe Conte. Nel dettaglio, è l'emendamento 5.020, firmato proprio da Delmastro, quello su cui si concentra l'ira del centrosinistra. Prevede che "benefici economici, contributi, borse di studio, provvidenze e ogni altra utilità comunque riconosciuti nell'ambito del diritto allo studio sono sospesi nei confronti dello studente che risulti sottoposto a indagini preliminari per uno dei delitti di cui agli articoli 336, 337, 339, 419, 420, 421, 421-bis, 582, 583 e 635 del codice penale, commessi nel corso o in occasione di manifestazioni, proteste od occupazioni, fino alla definizione del procedimento penale", si legge nel testo dell'emendamento. "Il Pubblico Ministero deve informare senza ritardo l'amministrazione che eroga il beneficio", scuola o università, "dell'iscrizione della notizia di reato". In caso di condanna, è prevista "la revoca del beneficio, con possibilità di restituzione in tutto o in parte delle somme già erogate per il periodo in cui si sono verificati i fatti. Nei casi di particolare gravità: esclusione dall'accesso ai benefici del diritto allo studio per i due anni accademici o scolastici successivi". Conte: "Basta un'accusa per perdere la borsa di studio" Per Conte, "sono le nuove frontiere della loro idea di sicurezza: colpire il diritto allo studio, intimidire chi manifesta, trasformare il dissenso in una colpa da sanzionare". Il leader del Movimento 5 Stelle si sofferma sul fatto che "tra i protagonisti di questa stretta c'è Andrea Delmastro. Proprio lui. Lo stesso Delmastro che ha beneficiato dello scudo parlamentare per negare alla Procura di Roma l'autorizzazione ad acquisire le chat con un prestanome della Camorra sugli affari in comune tramite una società di ristorazione", sottolinea Conte, che rincara: per gli studenti "basta un'accusa per perdere la borsa di studio. Delmastro e i fedelissimi di Meloni possono invece usare il Parlamento per scudarsi". Da qui la richiesta indirizzata alla presidente del Consiglio: "Cara Giorgia Meloni, se vuoi togliere benefici a indagati, inquisiti e condannati, non perdere tempo a cercarli nelle scuole e nelle università. Guarda dentro il tuo partito. Comincia dai tuoi sodali. Comincia da chi chiede repressione per gli studenti e pretende immunità per sé". Schlein: "Le borse di studio garantiscono maggiori opportunità" Per Elly Schlein l'emendamento di FdI si inserisce in quelle politiche con cui "le destre nel mondo hanno ucciso la speranza di un domani dignitoso alle giovani generazioni che ora protestano". "Ai giovani", continua la leader del Pd, "le borse di studio sono proprio quello strumento che ai giovani garantisce maggiori opportunità in un mondo sempre più diseguale. La destra dovrebbe interrogarsi sulle ragioni della protesta, anziché cercare nuovi strumenti per scoraggiarla". Grimaldi (Avs): "Delmastro garantista solo per le sue chat" Il vicecapogruppo di Avs alla Camera, Marco Grimaldi, attacca frontalmente Delmastro: "Pensa di fare il duro con i ragazzi, ma è garantista solo per le sue chat. È lo stesso che da sottosegretario alla Giustizia per dossieraggio contro le opposizioni ha passato a Donzelli i colloqui dal carcere di Sassari tra Cospito e gli altri detenuti al 41-bis, ed è stato condannato in primo grado a 8 mesi per rivelazione di segreto d'ufficio. È lo stesso che era socio al 25% della Bisteccheria d'Italia, amministrata da una diciottenne figlia di Mauro Caroccia, condannato in via definitiva per intestazione fittizia aggravata dal metodo mafioso, per vicende legate al clan dei Senese". Bonelli: "Si vuole punire chi protesta" E il leader rossoverde Angelo Bonelli chiosa: "Gli emendamenti di FdI sono roba da squallido regime. Un milione e mezzo di persone scende in piazza contro il carovita e il giorno dopo Fratelli d'Italia risponde con 27 emendamenti che hanno un solo obiettivo: punire chi protesta e spaventare chi vorrebbe farlo. È la logica di chi non tollera il dissenso e lo tratta come un reato".

articles.title: Non si sa come il “campo largo” voglia ripristinare il reddito di cittadinanza
articles.summary: I partiti di centrosinistra hanno raggiunto un accordo, ma restano da chiarire i destinatari della misura e le coperture economiche
articles.preview: Il 19 novembre diverse fonti stampa hanno dato la notizia secondo cui i partiti del “campo largo” avrebbero raggiunto un’intesa per inserire il ripristino del reddito di cittadinanza nel programma per le prossime elezioni politiche, previste nel 2027. Il “campo largo” è il nome con cui viene chiamata nel gergo giornalistico l’alleanza di centrosinistra formata da Partito Democratico, Movimento 5 Stelle e Alleanza Verdi-Sinistra, a cui si sono uniti di recente Italia Viva, Più Europa e Più Uno, il nuovo soggetto politico dell’ex direttore dell’Agenzia…
articles.body:
Il 19 novembre diverse fonti stampa hanno dato la notizia secondo cui i partiti del “campo largo” avrebbero raggiunto un’intesa per inserire il ripristino del reddito di cittadinanza nel programma per le prossime elezioni politiche, previste nel 2027. Il “campo largo” è il nome con cui viene chiamata nel gergo giornalistico l’alleanza di centrosinistra formata da Partito Democratico, Movimento 5 Stelle e Alleanza Verdi-Sinistra, a cui si sono uniti di recente Italia Viva, Più Europa e Più Uno, il nuovo soggetto politico dell’ex direttore dell’Agenzia delle entrate Ernesto Maria Ruffini.

Il tavolo della coalizione dedicato al lavoro ha dato il via libera a un testo condiviso sul “reddito minimo garantito”, la misura che entrerà nel programma comune in vista delle elezioni del 2027. La nuova denominazione richiama la raccomandazione del Consiglio dell’Unione europea del 30 gennaio 2023 sull’adeguatezza del reddito minimo e l’inclusione attiva, ma non è ancora chiaro nel dettaglio come funzionerebbe la misura.

Se da una parte i partiti del centrosinistra sembrano concordare sulla necessità di uno strumento più ampio per sostenere le persone in povertà, dall’altra restano da definire la platea dei beneficiari, i requisiti per accedere al sostegno e le risorse necessarie per finanziarlo.

articles.title: La classifica dei governi con cui abbiamo avuto più scioperi generali
articles.summary: Durante il governo Meloni si è registrato il maggior numero di scioperi generali nazionali, ma è durante il governo Draghi che sono stati più frequenti
articles.preview: Venerdì 20 novembre, in un centinaio di piazze italiane, lavoratori e studenti hanno manifestato per chiedere salari più alti, sicurezza sul lavoro e maggiori investimenti nei servizi pubblici. Con questo sciopero generale, proclamato dalla CGIL per protestare contro le politiche economiche del governo Meloni, si contano nove scioperi generali nazionali da inizio anno. E secondo il calendario della Commissione di garanzia sugli scioperi, altri due sono in programma per il prossimo 4 dicembre.
articles.body:
Venerdì 20 novembre, in un centinaio di piazze italiane, lavoratori e studenti hanno manifestato per chiedere salari più alti, sicurezza sul lavoro e maggiori investimenti nei servizi pubblici. Con questo sciopero generale, proclamato dalla CGIL per protestare contro le politiche economiche del governo Meloni, si contano nove scioperi generali nazionali da inizio anno. E secondo il calendario della Commissione di garanzia sugli scioperi, altri due sono in programma per il prossimo 4 dicembre. Ma quanti scioperi generali si sono svolti negli ultimi dieci anni? E qual è il governo sotto cui ne sono stati effettuati di più?

In breve, il governo Meloni è quello durante il quale si è svolto il maggior numero di scioperi generali nazionali, ma se si tiene conto della durata dei governi la classifica cambia. A seconda dell’esecutivo infatti si va da una media di uno sciopero generale ogni poco più di due settimane a uno ogni oltre tre mesi. E il governo Draghi è in testa a questa classifica.

articles.title: Sessantamila emendamenti alla manovra in dieci anni: quasi tutti finiscono carta straccia
articles.summary: I parlamentari ne presentano in media 6 mila all’anno, ma solo una piccola parte viene approvata. C’entrano i tempi di esame della manovra e il peso del governo
articles.preview: Come ogni anno in questo periodo, fa discutere la grande quantità di emendamenti presentati dai parlamentari al disegno di legge di Bilancio. Lo scorso 17 novembre è scaduto il termine per la presentazione degli emendamenti alla manovra per il 2027 in Commissione Bilancio alla Camera. Secondo fonti stampa, i vari gruppi parlamentari presenti alla Camera hanno presentato circa 6.600 proposte di modifica al testo.
articles.body:
Come ogni anno in questo periodo, fa discutere la grande quantità di emendamenti presentati dai parlamentari al disegno di legge di Bilancio. Lo scorso 17 novembre è scaduto il termine per la presentazione degli emendamenti alla manovra per il 2027 in Commissione Bilancio alla Camera. Secondo fonti stampa, i vari gruppi parlamentari presenti alla Camera hanno presentato circa 6.600 proposte di modifica al testo.

Abbiamo verificato e si tratta del numero più alto di emendamenti presentati in prima lettura a un disegno di legge di Bilancio nel corso di questa legislatura. L’anno scorso, in occasione del primo esame della manovra al Senato, erano stati 5.700, nel 2024 circa 4.500, nel 2023 3.300, mentre nel 2022 erano stati 3 mila. Quello di quest’anno non è comunque un primato dell’ultimo decennio: nel 2021, durante l’esame della legge di Bilancio per il 2022, approvata durante il governo Draghi, in Commissione Bilancio al Senato erano state presentate quasi 7.500 proposte di modifica. Nel complesso, secondo le nostre verifiche, dal 2016 a oggi i parlamentari hanno presentato quasi 60 mila emendamenti alla manovra, con una media di circa 6 mila emendamenti per ogni legge di Bilancio. Per calcolare il totale degli emendamenti abbiamo considerato quelli presentati nel primo ramo del Parlamento in cui viene esaminata la manovra, visto che di solito solo la prima camera riesce a modificare il disegno di legge di Bilancio.

articles.title: Questo video di Ronaldo al Pallone d’Oro con la bandiera della Palestina è falso
articles.summary: Il calciatore portoghese non era presente alla cerimonia del 2026, e nella scena ci sono diversi errori tipici dei programmi di IA generativa
articles.preview: Il 18 novembre 2026 su X è stato condiviso un video di Cristiano Ronaldo sul red carpet della cerimonia del Pallone d’Oro, uno dei più prestigiosi premi calcistici, mentra indossa la bandiera della Palestina e urla in spagnolo «Palestina libre, que vive Palestina» (ovvero, «Palestina libera, viva la Palestina»). Per questo, Ronaldo viene portato via da due agenti della polizia. L’autore del post applaude il comportamento di Ronaldo, definendolo «MITICOOO». È un video creato con l’intelligenza artificiale, che diffonde una notizia falsa.
articles.body:
Il 18 novembre 2026 su X è stato condiviso un video di Cristiano Ronaldo sul red carpet della cerimonia del Pallone d’Oro, uno dei più prestigiosi premi calcistici, mentra indossa la bandiera della Palestina e urla in spagnolo «Palestina libre, que vive Palestina» (ovvero, «Palestina libera, viva la Palestina»). Per questo, Ronaldo viene portato via da due agenti della polizia.

L’autore del post applaude il comportamento di Ronaldo, definendolo «MITICOOO».

È un video creato con l’intelligenza artificiale, che diffonde una notizia falsa.

Nessun media ha riportato la presunta notizia del calciatore portoghese portato via dalle forze dell’ordine durante la cerimonia di assegnazione del Pallone d’Oro, tenutasi il 26 ottobre 2026 al Palladium Theatre di Londra, per aver espresso solidarietà alla Palestina. Tra l’altro, Ronaldo non era presente alla cerimonia.

Il video infatti è stato creato con un programma di intelligenza artificiale generativa, come si può notare da alcuni dettagli che non corrispondono alla realtà e da alcuni errori nella scena. Ad esempio, nel backdrop del red carpet reale erano disegnati anche i loghi degli sponsor, e non solo del Pallone d’Oro (come si vede invece nel video falso), e i fotografi sullo sfondo non erano posizionati sotto al backdrop, ma di fronte, oltre il red carpet. Tra l’altro, le figure dei fotografi sono indistinguibili tra di loro, e restano immobili per tutto il filmato.

A pubblicare originariamente il contenuto IA è stato, il 13 novembre 2026, l’account TikTok “Cristiano Ronaldo fans” (@zazahamza32) che pubblica esclusivamente deepfake del calciatore portoghese in sostegno della Palestina, come specificato in biografia.

Sul video TikTok è presente il watermark di Sora – il generatore di video IA di OpenAI – una piccola nuvoletta animata con gli occhi e la scritta “Sora”, che contrassegna la natura artificiale della scena. Il video in analisi è stato dunque editato per evitare che si vedesse il watermark.

articles.title: Russia-bound ship towed away after it was attacked in Gulf of Finland
articles.summary: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone strike on Saturday. Kyiv has yet to comment.
articles.preview: A Russian cargo vessel that was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland is being towed away, authorities have said. The the Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, sparking a fire aboard. It then drifted into Finnish waters and its crew were evacuated to Russia. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.
articles.body:
A Russian cargo vessel that was hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland is being towed away, authorities have said.

The the Sparta II had been bound for Russia's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad when it was hit on Saturday morning, sparking a fire aboard.

It then drifted into Finnish waters and its crew were evacuated to Russia. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment.

Finland's Border Guard said on Sunday afternoon that fire was no longer visible from the outside but thermal cameras showed that some containers on the ship were still warm.

The Sparta II was "slightly listing", Finnish authorities added, but the "situation is stable" and no fuel or other "hazardous substance leaks" had been detected.

Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones appeared to have been used in the strike and that there was "no threat" to his territory's supplies.

The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments.

The company says it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex.

Finland's coast guard said it had been alerted to the attack at around 08:50 local time (06:50 GMT) on Saturday and that the cargo vessel had been located approximately 50km west of the island of Suursaari in the Gulf of Finland.

This prompted "temporary aviation and maritime restrictions" around the area, Finnish border officials said.

"War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor."

Shortly after the incident, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian helicopter was suspected of violating the country's airspace, potentially linked to "rescue or tracking operations".

While Besprozvannykh initially said the crew of the Sparta II intended to repair the ship and carry on their journey, the Finnish Border Guard later said they had been evacuated to another Russian vessel that was en route to Russia.

Jukka-Pekka Lumilahti, director of maritime operations at the Finnish Border Guard, said during a news conference on Sunday that one Sparta II crew member had suffered minor injuries.

The Russian rescue vessel Murman is leading towing operations with the support of a Finnish guard ship and a Estonian naval patrol vessel.

Kaliningrad is a Russian exclave that sits between Poland and Lithuania.

Finnish Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said that the Border Guard was responsible for the investigation into the attack and was co-operating with other relevant authorities.

Nato has also been informed, the defence ministry said.

The Baltic Sea has become a flashpoint in the Russia-Ukraine war, triggered when Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Ukraine has recently ramped up its long-range attacks against Russia beyond the front lines.

Earlier this month, a Ukrainian drone strike hit a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland.

articles.title: Explosion on Russian ship at Libya port caused by suspected drone attack, officials say
articles.summary: Libya's eastern government says the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia.
articles.preview: An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said. The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government. It added that the site was secured, and there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.
articles.body:
An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base port was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said.

The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libyan state media reported, citing the eastern government.

It added that the site was secured, and there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment.

Satellite imagery from Planet Labs PBC, reviewed by BBC Verify, shows a boat on fire at 0547 GMT at the Benghazi port, with a separate image captured several hours later appearing to show the same vessel partially submerged.

Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship engulfed in flames and smoke, while it is still dark.

The eastern-based Government of National Stability (GNS) said the Russian ship was using the Benghazi port within the framework of an existing maritime agreement.

Sunday's incident is under investigation, and authorities are coordinating with their Russian counterparts to determine the source of the suspected attack and who is responsible for it, GNS added.

GNS condemned the attack on a ship inside a Libyan port, and called it a violation of maritime safety and an attack on their sovereignty. It said Libya was not party to the Russia-Ukraine war, or any other conflict beyond its borders.

Separately, Libya's internationally recognised government in Tripoli - the Government of National Unity (GNU) - warned against hosting foreign forces and allowing them to use facilities in a statement published by state media.

GNU said such activity raises "serious fears" about "risks that may result from involving ports and civilian facilities in activities related to external conflicts, and the resulting threat to the lives of citizens and the safety of national facilities and assets".

Libya fractured into violence and instability after its leader Muammar Gaddafi was overthrown in 2011, leading to the opposing governments.

Benghazi is more than 2,000 km (1,243 miles) away from the Russian capital Moscow.

articles.title: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
articles.summary: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says Iran's navy said on Sunday that two supertankers hit naval mines and caught fire after entering a "restricted area" east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported. According to the Fars news agency, the navy said the tankers had switched off their detection and navigation systems and struck the mines north of Ghanam Island. Both vessels reportedly stopped moving. Supertankers usually carry two million barrels of oil or more, about twice as much as a standard tanker. The navy also warned that relying on "smugglers such as CENTCOM", referring to US Central Command, would result in "nothing but heavy losses". UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) also said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman. It gave no further details, saying only that authorities were aware and an investigation was under way. It was unclear whether the incident involved either of the tankers Iran described. British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh swam in the waters of the Strait of Hormuz to highlight the "devastating environmental consequences of war" on 21 November 2026 (Lewis Pugh Foundation / AFP)

articles.title: From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah
articles.summary: From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah Submitted by Fayha Shalash on Sun, 11/22/2026 - 13:25 The attacks come amid a sharp rise in settler violence during the olive harvest, with the UN documenting a record 467 incidents in October An Israeli settler stands between Israeli forces and Palestinians protesting an alleged arson attack in Idna, west of Hebron, occupied West Bank, 5 June 2026 (Hazem Bader/AFP) Off In a series of coordinated attacks across several villages near the city of Ramallah in the central occupied West Bank, Israeli settlers torched Palestinian vehicles between Saturday evening and Sunday morning. The settlers also spray-painted racist slogans on the walls of homes in the three villages, calling for the killing of Arabs and for revenge against them. Rafat Abu Musa, head of the village council of Deir al-Sudan, north of Ramallah, told Middle East Eye that settlers infiltrated the southern part of the village at 11.30pm on Saturday and burned down two vehicles. The settlers spray-painted slogans in Hebrew on the walls of nearby houses, he said, adding that the same area had been targeted by a similar attack two months ago, during which a vehicle was set on fire. The settlers, he said, came from a newly built outpost on the summit of Jabal al-Ras, located in the neighbouring village of Umm Safa. "The fire department was delayed in reaching the scene because they require coordination with the Israeli army; by the time they arrived, the vehicles had already been reduced to ashes," he said. According to Abu Musa, some five months ago, the settlers seized "an entire mountain" in the southern part of the village, where they established an outpost and constructed roads. The outpost has deprived residents of access to more than half of the village’s olive trees, as settlers assault the residents and prevent them from approaching their own land, he said. "This fierce onslaught is being directed by extremist Israeli ministers; these are systematic and recurring attacks," Abu Musa said. The area where the vehicles were torched is classified as 'Area A'. Under the Oslo Accords, the region is supposed to be under exclusive Palestinian control. Fake investigations A few hours after the attack in Abu Musa's village, settlers set fire to seven vehicles in the town of Kafr Malik, east of Ramallah. More than ten settlers infiltrated the northern part of the town, arriving from an outpost they had established between Kafr Malik and al-Mughayyir; a journey that required them to trek for at least an hour along a rugged mountain path, Jihad Qaq, a resident, told Middle East Eye. 'Jewish terrorism in every sense': Eisenkot blames Smotrich and Ben Gvir for settler attacks the vehicles on fire and wrote racist slogans on the walls of the houses before withdrawing. "An hour after the attack, the Israeli army stormed the town, forced the civil defence crews who were in the process of extinguishing the fires to leave and drove away the residents." "They conducted an investigation, but then withdrew without any results," Qaq said. He said that the village is constantly subjected to harassment by settlers, who, a year and a half ago, burned vehicles in the southern part of the area and killed three young men. "Settler herders have prevented more than 70 percent of the Palestinian olive harvesters from reaching their land this year, assaulting and beating them," he said. According to data from the Commission Against the Wall and Settlements, attacks by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank saw a marked increase this past October, coinciding with the olive harvest season. Settlers carried out 1,369 attacks during the month, a 112 percent rise compared to September, which saw 647 such incidents. Relentless attacks Meanwhile, in the eastern part of the village of Deir Abu Mashal west of Ramallah, classified as 'Area B', settlers burned eight vehicles and wrote racist slogans. Jamil Musa, head of the village council, said that the settlers arrived from an outpost they had established a few months ago, one of several such outposts they have set up in the vicinity of the village. Israeli settlers kill Palestinian grandmother in her home in Jericho 30am, and the group, consisting of eight to 10 individuals, withdrew from the village after painting racist slogans. "The Israeli army raided the village and promised to launch an investigation, but nothing has come of it. They also told us that the Israeli police would follow up, but they have yet to arrive," he stated. Two months ago, settlers set fire to vehicles in the village. In June 2025, they assaulted several families and beat five young men, leaving them with serious injuries. Residents are unable to access nearly half of the village’s land for the olive harvest due to attacks by settlers, who have been assaulting Palestinians farmers. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) documented 467 settler attacks that resulted in injuries or property damage during the month of October alone, the highest monthly figure since the organisation began tracking such incidents in 2006. Over the course of the year, from the beginning of January through 19 October, Ocha recorded 2,159 settler attacks, an average of 7.4 incidents per day, compared to a daily average of five attacks throughout 2025. According to Ocha, these attacks were particularly concentrated during the olive harvest season. Between 1 September and 19 October, 272 attacks linked to the harvest were recorded, resulting in the killing of one Palestinian, injuries to 200 others and the destruction of more than 3,200 olive trees. articles.summary: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia An explosion on a Russian ship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya’s eastern-based government has said. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the suspected strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the frontlines. articles.preview: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia An explosion on a Russian ship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya’s eastern-based government has said. There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the suspected strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the frontlines. Continue reading...
articles.body:
An explosion on a Russian ship docked at the naval base in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya’s eastern-based government has said.

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the suspected strike, but it comes as Ukrainian forces have stepped up their long-range barrages against Russia far beyond the frontlines.

“Initial investigations indicate that the explosion occurred onboard a Russian ship docked in the port,” said the administration backed by the military commander Khalifa Haftar. “It is suspected that the ship was attacked by drones.”

Authorities in divided Libya’s east said the vessel had stopped at Benghazi port to refuel and resupply on its way back to Russia, under maritime cooperation agreements between the two countries.

Two medical sources said no deaths had been reported from the blast, but there were injuries. The number and nationalities of those injured are not yet known.

There was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities, and no one has claimed responsibility for the suspected attack.

The eastern-based Libyan authority said port and naval base facilities, including warehouses, were safe and that normal operations would resume once the fire was brought under control and the site secured.

It condemned the suspected attack as a violation of Libya’s sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety, saying it would take legal and diplomatic measures against anyone found responsible.

“The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts,” it said.

If it is confirmed that Ukraine has been able to blow up or seriously damage a Russian warship in Benghazi, it would represent one of its most successful naval strikes during the five-year war.

But it also represents a risky extension of the fighting far beyond eastern Europe, in an incident that could affect civilians in another continent and the working of the port.

A small unit of Ukrainian special forces operatives has been based at Misrata, western Libya, and is believed to have coordinated drone attacks on Russian tankers and transport ships in the past year.

Initial reports and footage suggest the ship was struck from above, potentially by a drone, launched no more than a few kilometres away from the target in port.

Russia is close to the Benghazi authorities that control eastern Libya. It uses the port to supply Russian mercenary forces in Africa and as a base in the Mediterranean, which has a growing importance after it lost bases in Syria.

Separately, a fire onboard a Russian cargo ship that was struck by drones in the Baltic Sea continued to smoulder on Sunday, Finland’s border guard said, with emergency services from Finland, Russia and Estonia working together to put out the blaze.

The Finnish military said the strike on the Sparta II on Saturday was probably carried out by Ukraine and that the vessel later drifted into Finnish waters, where it remained at anchor. The 16 crew members were evacuated on to a nearby Russian ship. One crew member was slightly injured.

On Sunday visible flames had been put out, with operations focusing on cooling down the containers and stabilising the vessel, Finnish authorities said.

Pictures and video released earlier by the Finnish coastguard showed several vessels spraying the Sparta II with water cannons during the night in an attempt to put out the flames and cool down containers stacked on its deck.

The ship, bound for the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, had been damaged in international waters west of Russia’s Gogland Island, Finland’s defence forces said, corroborating an account by Russian officials.

“Smoke is still coming from the vessel, and there is clearly still heat onboard,” said Jukka-Pekka Lumilahti, a sea safety officer and commander of the maritime sub-centre Helsinki for the Finnish border guard, at a press conference on Sunday.

Kyiv has sent waves of military drones towards the Leningrad region on Russia’s north-west coast this year, including some that strayed into the airspace of nearby Baltic countries, leading to fears that the war was spilling on to Nato territory.

The risk of further attacks in the Gulf of Finland, a narrow arm of the Baltic Sea, could not be ruled out, Ivo Värk, the Estonian navy commander, told the public broadcaster ERR on Sunday.

Finland’s military said last week it had detected a strike on a Russian warship in the same area during Ukrainian drone attacks.

articles.title: Sánchez apela en la recta final de la campaña al voto joven para lograr otra remontada como en 2023
articles.summary: El presidente ondea la bandera de Murcia tras ser declarado ‘persona non grata’ por el Parlamento regional en otro acto multitudinario
articles.preview: El presidente ondea la bandera de Murcia tras ser declarado ‘persona non grata’ por el Parlamento regional en otro acto multitudinario El voto joven se ha convertido en la última frontera que puede decantar las elecciones. Más de 1,6 millones de adolescentes que han cumplido la mayoría de edad desde las generales de 2023 se podrán estrenar en las urnas el 29-N.
articles.body:
El presidente ondea la bandera de Murcia tras ser declarado ‘persona non grata’ por el Parlamento regional en otro acto multitudinario

El voto joven se ha convertido en la última frontera que puede decantar las elecciones. Más de 1,6 millones de adolescentes que han cumplido la mayoría de edad desde las generales de 2023 se podrán estrenar en las urnas el 29-N. El PSOE les ha dedicado el mitin de Murcia —que ha desbordado las previsiones más optimistas con unas 10.000 personas— en su pugna con Vox por un electorado en el que la ultraderecha ha encontrado uno de sus grandes caladeros entre el público masculino. Para convencerles, Pedro Sánchez ha repasado su gestión y compartido el “orgullo” por los 2.600 millones que el Gobierno destina a becas y que permiten que haya más de un millón de estudiantes becados: “Para que estudien lo que quieran, con independencia del tamaño del bolsillo de sus padres y madres”.

Un ejemplo, de la decena que ha puesto, con los que ha apelado a concentrar el voto progresista en el PSOE y también de aquellos votantes moderados desideologizados que no quieren a Santiago Abascal como vicepresidente del Gobierno. “Pido a toda la España que quiera avanzar que vote todo al rojo, al PSOE, el 29-N para lograr un Gobierno progresista. Ellos —por PP y Vox— no son dos derechas, no nos equivoquemos, son una única involución. Y solo hay una papeleta para derrotar a esa coalición reaccionaria”, ha animado el presidente del Gobierno enfundado en una camiseta con el lema La fuerza de la juventud.

Con el foco en el electorado de menos edad pero sin olvidarse del femenino, el puntal del PSOE, el presidente también ha destacado el 1,2 millón “de chavales” que estudian Formación Profesional en otro mitin convertido en una fiesta, donde las llamadas a lograr una nueva “remontada” como la de 2023 y las de Lula en Brasil y de los demócratas en Estados Unidos contra Donald Trump no sonaban imposibles para un público entregado pese a lo que dicen la mayoría de encuestas. Y a los que no son tan jóvenes, Sánchez les ha recordado que en sus ocho años en La Moncloa ha subido los permisos de paternidad de 5 a 19 semanas. “¡Eso significa 100 días más para que los padres y madres disfruten de la infancia de sus hijos!“, ha clamado en un acto multitudinario. Varios miles de simpatizantes y militantes se han resignado a seguirlo fuera en una pantalla gigante, justo en un bastión de la derecha y a un par de kilómetros de donde Alberto Núñez Feijóo también mitineaba.

Con una capacidad para entre 4.000 y 5.000 personas si el tipo incluye el uso de la pista, como sucede con los mítines, el pabellón escogido se ha quedado pequeño. El fenómeno no es nuevo en los actos del PSOE. Fuentes de la organización explicaban, mientras la cola para entrar casi daba la vueta entera al recinto, que habían movilizado a menos de 2.000 militantes en autobuses. “Lo que está pasando no es normal”, confiaban sin esconder su sorpresa. ”En cada mercado, en cada pueblo, por donde vamos, es impresionante. Yo no he visto en mi vida una campaña así, con un pabellón así y con tanta gente que se ha quedado fuera”, ha resumido María González Veracruz, cabeza de lista al Congreso, el ambiente que los socialistas palpan en la calle, en los repartos de propaganda, y ni qué decir en sus mítines desde la precampaña. Los gritos de “¡Sí se puede, sí se puede!“, que eran característicos de Podemos, han atronado varias veces.

“Hemos reventado este estadio con la fuerza de la juventud que va a parar al fascismo en las urnas el 29-N”, ha reivindicado Aránzazu Figueroa, secretaria general de Juventudes Socialistas y el rostro de la campaña en redes del canal La fuerza de la gente inspirado en el Ejército digital de Lula. La referencia a la ultraderecha tenía toda la intencionalidad, como un vídeo proyectado para incitar al voto joven en recuerdo de “los abuelos de muchos” represaliados por el franquismo. La formación de Santiago Abascal es la primera opción entre los votantes de 18 a 24 años por 3 puntos —22,1% por un 19%— sobre la candidatura de Sánchez, según el CIS preelectoral de octubre. El margen se reduce entre los 25 y 34 años —21,4% por 18,8%— y la ventaja de Vox se reduce a un punto y medio —22,9% por 21,4%— en la capa de edad de 35 a 44 años.

El PP cierra el podio entre la juventud, con una horquilla entre el 11,6% y el 13,8%. Por ese motivo, Sánchez ha enfocado su intervención en “seguir avanzando” en políticas de vivienda y derechos laborales “para dar un futuro a los jóvenes”. “Estoy convencido de que confiarán de forma mayoritaria en el PSOE”, ha remachado el presidente, que ha seguido buena parte del acto sentado entre veinteañeros que van en las listas del PSOE en toda España. “Durante mucho tiempo nos han hecho pensar que por ganar 1.500 euros, tener una PlayStation o comprarnos un iphone a plazos éramos clase media. Que nuestros intereses eran los de los ricos”, ha intervenido el murciano Miguel Ortega. “La educación pública es el mayor ascensor social que tenemos”, ha sido el mensaje de la andaluza Martina López, que se ha declarado “garrapatera orgullosa pese a lo que diga Ayuso”.

El voto femenino también es esencial para el PSOE y, muy en particular, el de las más jóvenes, que se han mantenido fieles a los socialistas y sus postulados frente a la hegemonía que ha logrado Vox mientras los más jóvenes se derechizaban. Los socialistas recuerdan en todos sus mítines que Feijóo ya ha anunciado que eliminará el Ministerio de Igualdad, que pretende revisar el derecho al aborto, ya que no comparte que las adolescentes de 16 y 17 años puedan tomar esa decisión sin la aprobación de sus padres, mientras que la ultraderecha sigue negándose a reconocer como tal la violencia de género y se refiere a la violencia machista como violencia intrafamiliar. “Pido el voto de las mujeres porque sabéis muy bien los recortes del Estado del Bienestar por la desigualdad estructural que sufrís; si alguien nos va a dar la victoria son las mujeres de España”, les ha interpelado.

Con la bandera de Murcia

Sánchez ha ondeado la bandera de Murcia en el mitin en un gesto de un enorme significado, ya que el Parlamento regional declaró al presidente a principios de noviembre persona non grata con los votos de PP y Vox. “Murcia es una grandísima tierra y los murcianos son gente gratísima. No me insultan a mí, sino a cualquiera que se les pone delante. De estas elecciones vamos a hacer también un referéndum entre la buena política y la mala educación”, ha aseverado.

El candidato del PSOE ondeó la bandera de España hace una semana en Alcorcón y el martes en Albacete. “Lo que me dicen me recuerda la canción de Loquillo La Mala reputación”, ha dicho, en referencia a la versión española de la canción de George Brassens: “Haga lo que haga, todo les parece mal, viene a decir. Si subimos el salario mínimo, mal. Si cuidamos con 700 millones el Mar Menor, mal. Si revalorizamos las pensiones, mal”, ha abundado. Antes que Sánchez, Francisco Lucas, delegado del Gobierno y secretario general autonómico, ha tachado un cartel que rezaba ese Persona non grata entre vítores. “¡Qué orgullo que nunca os habéis rendido!“, ha apreciado.

La última vez que el PSOE fue primera fuerza en unas generales en Murcia sucedió en 2019 debido a la división del voto de la derecha. Los socialistas se impusieron con tres escaños —como en 2023 pero lejos de los 5 asientos que lograba en los años ochenta—, por delante del triple empate de PP, Vox y Ciudadanos con dos diputados. En 2023, el bloque conservador se impuso llevándose 6 de los 10 escaños en juego. Una ventaja que PP y Vox confían en aumentar llevándose el diputado que Sumar obtuvo hace tres años.

Al finalizar el mitin, un tablón de la grada más cercana a la zona de prensa se ha levantado y una mujer ha caído por el hueco. Los servicios de emergencia, que estaban a pocos metros, la han atendido en pocos segundos tras sufrir una caída de alrededor de un metro. La asistente al acto se ha ido por su propio pie, sin mayores consecuencias.

articles.title: Israel: Eisenkot and Netanyahu parties meet again for unity government talks
articles.summary: Israel: Eisenkot and Netanyahu parties meet again for unity government talks Representatives from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and the party of his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar, met on Sunday to discuss forming a unity government, Haaretz is reporting . The meeting follows earlier talks last Sunday after nearly a month of deadlock in the Israeli Knesset since October's election, which saw no party gain an overall majority. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have so far failed to negotiate a viable coalition government alongside smaller parties. Absent from Sunday's meeting were representatives of Naftali Bennett's Together party, which received the third-largest vote share and attended the previous round of talks.

articles.body:
Japan’s education ministry has compiled measures to strengthen the functions of kōsen technical colleges, featuring plans to expand their educational scope to agriculture and increase financial support for new kōsen colleges.

With advances in artificial intelligence and other technologies expected to lead to a future shortage of professionals in science, engineering and digital fields, the ministry aims to encourage the establishment of more kōsen colleges to train engineers.

Kōsen are five-year higher educational institutions that students can enter after graduating from junior high school. According to the ministry, there are a total of 58 national, public and private technical colleges across Japan.

The current standards for establishing kōsen colleges, which stipulate requirements such as the number of teachers and the size of school grounds, contain no provisions for departments outside the industrial field.

To expand the scope of kōsen education, the ministry plans to introduce similar provisions for agricultural departments. It is also considering adding fields related to content creation, such as manga and anime, in response to demand.

The ministry will expand financial support for local governments and other entities seeking to establish new kōsen colleges. It plans to raise the maximum amount of subsidies to ¥4 billion from the current ¥2 billion. Nagano, Aichi and Shiga prefectures are among those taking steps to establish new kōsen colleges.

Regarding the academic title of “associate,” awarded to kōsen college graduates, the ministry is considering treating it as an internationally recognized degree.

articles.title: Juan Atkins da Detroit allo spazio profondo
articles.summary: Model 500 nel 1995 ha trasformato il funk in un viaggio nel futuro. Deep space racchiude tutte le ambizioni e le contraddizioni della techno

articles.body:
Quando ascoltiamo la techno, difficilmente pensiamo a chi ha inventato quel linguaggio, agli esseri umani che ci sono dietro. Il suono delle macchine, il ronzio di fondo del sistema, quella vertigine postumana, che trasforma anche noi che balliamo in macchine senzienti, ci trascina lontano. La morte di Juan Atkins, avvenuta il 31 ottobre a Città del Messico, ci ricorda invece quanto questa musica, questo suono e quest’estetica si debbano a una persona precisa: un giovane musicista afroamericano cresciuto a Detroit che, tra la fine degli anni settanta e l’inizio degli ottanta, cominciò a immaginarsi un nuovo suono. Il soprannome The originator, l’inventore, gli è rimasto addosso per tutta la vita.

La Detroit di quegli anni era la tomba del sogno industriale, della modernità com’era stata costruita nel novecento: una città di rovine, di povertà vecchie e nuove e di quartieri segregati. E Juan Atkins non lavorava in una bolla: viveva in uno di quei quartieri e alla radio ascoltava un dj noto con il nome di The Electrifying Mojo, che accostava Parliament-Funkadelic e Kraftwerk, rendendo porosi dei confini che solo l’industria discografica considerava invalicabili.

Quel programma radiofonico era stato fondamentale anche per un altro artista del Midwest: un tale Prince Rogers Nelson, di Minneapolis. Più tardi Atkins, insieme a Derrick May e Kevin Saunderson, avrebbe dato forma alla techno di Detroit: una delle tante invenzioni afroamericane destinate a cambiare il modo di ballare del mondo. E a essere cannibalizzate da un’industria bianca.

Il successo internazionale della house di Chicago e della techno di Detroit ha spesso messo in ombra le condizioni molto locali in cui quella musica era nata. Nel suo saggio Assembling a black counter culture (Primary Information 2022), DeForrest Brown Jr. ricostruisce il conflitto tra l’autonomia dei giovani produttori di Detroit e i circuiti discografici statunitensi ed europei.

I secondi furono molto più rapidi dei primi a capire le potenzialità commerciali di quel genere di musica. Brown descrive il progetto di Underground Resistance, il collettivo della generazione successiva, come “un’impresa produttiva autogestita”: fabbricare e distribuire i propri dischi, dare voce agli abitanti neri della città e riportare opportunità nella comunità.

Il futuro tecnologico aveva bisogno anche d’infrastrutture, soldi e controllo sui mezzi per realizzarlo: Juan Atkins e gli altri lo capirono subito. Alla fine è la vecchia idea marxista del controllo dei mezzi di produzione. E di distribuzione.

E ai mezzi di produzione è ispirato il nome del progetto più famoso di Juan Atkins: Model 500, un nome che è un po’ uno pseudonimo dietro cui nascondersi e un po’ un marchio di fabbrica. Con quel nome, nel 1995, Atkins avrebbe firmato il suo album più ambizioso e sfaccettato: Deep space. Non una raccolta di singoli, come spesso avveniva nella musica dance, ma un vero album con una sua sequenza, un suo andamento e una sua estetica.

Model 500, The flow, 1995

La politica e la poetica di Atkins passavano soprattutto dall’immaginazione. In Più brillante del sole, pubblicato originariamente nel 1998 e tradotto da Alessandro Mazzi per Nero, lo scrittore britannico di origini ghanesi Kodwo Eshun scrive: “Il nome Model 500 annuncia il produttore come modello prossimo venturo, il sintetizzatore del futuro”.

Quel nome da apparecchio elettronico consentiva d’inventarsi un’identità, di sottrarsi alle aspettative su ciò che un musicista nero dovesse rappresentare. Per Eshun, “technificare significa sintetizzare la musica dagli stessi ritmi robotici che hanno messo fuori uso gli umani di Detroit”.

Le macchine che avevano trasformato il lavoro industriale fino a divorarlo diventavano strumenti per progettare un’altra esistenza. Era questo capovolgimento della macchina, da strumento di oppressione a motore per viaggiare verso un nuovo futuro, a improntare il lavoro di Juan Atkins. Viaggiare, o forse migrare.

La musica di Deep space ci ricorda anche oggi, a più di trent’anni di distanza e nel dibattito sulle intelligenze artificiali, che le macchine possiamo riprendercele, sabotarle, farle nostre: strapparle di mano a chi vorrebbe farne l’ennesimo strumento di sorveglianza e di sfruttamento.

Dipingere però la techno di Detroit solo come un’utopia libertaria e rivoluzionaria sarebbe un po’ riduttivo. Nel suo saggio “Dance dance revolution?”, pubblicato su The Baffler, lo scrittore e regista Hubert Adjei-Kontoh ci fa riflettere sulle fratture di classe interne alla prima scena di Detroit, frequentata anche da ragazzi della borghesia nera che volevano tenere lontani dai loro party i coetanei poveri.

Erano state le conquiste sindacali dell’industria automobilistica della città a creare il benessere necessario per sperimentare. Se un ragazzo nero di Detroit poteva comprarsi un sintetizzatore Korg MS-10, molto spesso alle spalle aveva una famiglia di operai specializzati che avevano raggiunto un certo livello, per quanto fragile, di benessere. È un paradosso da tenere presente: riconoscere la storia nera della techno di Detroit significa anche prendere sul serio le sue contraddizioni.

In Europa la techno trovò un mercato più ricettivo. Deep space, infatti, uscì per la R&S, un’etichetta belga nata a Gand nel 1983 su iniziativa di Renaat Vandepapeliere e Sabine Maes. Vandepapeliere chiamò i numeri di telefono stampati sulle etichette di quei dischi pazzeschi e futuristici che arrivavano da Detroit. In questo modo entrò in contatto con i padri fondatori della techno: Juan Atkins, Derrick May e Kevin Saunderson. Quegli scambi contribuirono a creare un ponte culturale tra Detroit e l’Europa.

Una musica mai sentita prima

La ricchezza di suoni e la dinamica di Deep space sono sconvolgenti: ascoltarlo nel 1995 significava avvicinarsi a una musica mai sentita prima. Ancora oggi fa lo stesso effetto. La cassa regolare tiene la rotta, mentre tutto intorno si muovono bassi elastici, percussioni secche e linee di sintetizzatore che allargano l’orizzonte.

L’eredità electro degli anni ottanta sembra sublimarsi in un suono più spazioso, dove la precisione delle sequenze lascia respirare le melodie. La parola techno rischia di far pensare soltanto a qualcosa di robotico, d’industriale, di asettico e artificiale. Qui invece la macchina riesce a sognare e a immaginare se stessa come qualcosa di organico, quasi fosse uscita da un romanzo di Philip K. Dick.

Nella musica una figura torna e cambia significato, un ritmo ostinato diventa un ambiente da abitare. A fare da motore immobile di tutto è soprattutto il funk, che ci ancora alla realtà anche quando la musica sembra lanciarsi nello spazio. Model 500 non fa che proporci una versione aumentata e aggiornata della Mothership, l’astronave madre con cui, negli anni settanta, i Parliament-Funkadelic partivano per il loro viaggio afrofuturistico e liberatorio nello spazio.

Gran parte dell’album nasce dalla collaborazione con Moritz von Oswald, percussionista, compositore e figura centrale della scena berlinese. La techno di Deep space è fatta da musicisti che s’incontrano, condividono strumenti e lavorano sul suono.

Nel 2013 Atkins ricordava su Electronic Beats la meraviglia provata davanti al sistema con cui von Oswald sincronizzava vecchie apparecchiature di marche diverse. Dietro a quel viaggio cosmico c’è anche questo: trovare il modo di far dialogare e interagire tra loro delle macchine. Allora sembrava fantascienza, oggi è la nostra quotidianità.

Riascoltato dopo la morte di Atkins, Deep space conserva una strana forma di familiarità, quasi d’intimità. Il futuro che immaginava è diventato in parte il nostro paesaggio sonoro, ma l’album mantiene aperta una possibilità che oggi facciamo fatica a vedere: usare la tecnologia per fabbricarsi una vita diversa e una visione dell’universo più vasta, anziché una prigione. Un giovane musicista di Detroit si era costruito un’astronave con i suoi sintetizzatori. Trent’anni dopo possiamo ancora salirci per partire alla scoperta dello spazio profondo. ◆

articles.title: Nigerian youth have shown their power in the past - why aren't they shaping this election?
articles.summary: Fewer young people have registered to vote in next year's election than in 2023 - are young people losing faith in democracy?
articles.preview: Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics. At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40. He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections. "Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC. But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.
articles.body:
Abdulhadi Dalhatu is something of a rarity in Nigeria politics.

At 38, he is among the young people seeking elected office in a country where about 80% of the population is under 40.

He hopes his age will stand in his favour as he campaigns for a seat in the state assembly in the northern Kano state in January's general elections.

"Younger people are the majority in this country and should be deciding the future," Dalhatu tells the BBC.

But Nigeria's political history suggests he faces an uphill battle.

Since the return to civilian rule in 1999, Goodluck Jonathan has been the youngest person elected president, taking office at the age of 53.

The current president, Bola Tinubu, is 74 and would be 79 by the end of a second term if he is re-elected in January.

His main challengers are also considerably older. Atiku Abubakar, seeking the presidency for the seventh time, is 79, while Peter Obi is 65.

Of the 18 presidential candidates, only one is under 40 - Moses Olusoji Adebisi, a 35-year-old businessman representing the Democratic Leadership Alliance (DLA).

Although he says he is confident of winning, few Nigerians appear to know much about him and he has not been seen much on the campaign trail.

The contrast is striking in a country with one of the world's youngest populations, where young people have repeatedly demonstrated their ability to shape political debate and mobilise for change.

In the previous election, Obi, then 61, galvanised millions of young Nigerians through a social media-driven movement known as the "Obedients".

His campaign promised a break from the established political order, appealing particularly to young people struggling to find jobs and earn a decent living.

But his failure to win the presidency left many of his supporters disillusioned.

"At the time we were so hopeful, but unfortunately the result wasn't what we wanted, which made many lose hope in the system," former Obedient Nonso Chukwudi tells the BBC.

The movement had built on the momentum of the EndSars protests in 2020, which grew into one of Nigeria's biggest youth-led movement in decades.

Initially sparked by anger over police brutality, the demonstrators developed into a wider call for political reform, accountability and greater youth participation in governance.

But the protests were eventually crushed by the authorities. About 56 were reportedly killed, although officials dispute this figure, while hundreds were arrested and some had their bank accounts frozen.

Both EndSars and the Obedients demonstrated the capacity of young Nigerians to mobilise around political causes.

But turning that enthusiasm into sustained electoral participation has proved much harder.

Hajara Musa, 33, is among those who have lost faith in the political system. She has no plans to register or vote in the near future.

"I just feel like things are already determined and I'll just be wasting my time. It is going to be the same people all over again," she tells the BBC.

The electoral register appears to reflect this growing disillusionment.

Although the number of registered voters has increased by 10 million to over 103 million since the last election, enrolment of those under 35 has actually fallen, by about seven million.

Young people now account for just 29% of registered voters, down from 40% in 2023.

Nigeria's electoral commission, Inec, says it has made efforts to encourage more young people to register ahead of the 2027 general elections.

This includes appointing nine ambassadors from the entertainment industry, spanning film, music and comedy, to reach younger audiences.

But the figures suggest these efforts have yet to make a significant difference.

Dalhatu says he understands the frustration but argues that young Nigerians cannot expect change, if they stay away from the political process.

"Unfortunately, many prefer to just post on social media" instead of getting involved, he says.

Of course being young does not mean you are necessarily the best candidate.

For those who want to participate, there is a formidable obstacle to getting into politics - money.

Dalhatu dreams of becoming president one day, but says he has previously had to abandon campaigns because he could not raise enough funds.

The cost of running for office in Nigeria is notoriously high.

Under the Electoral Act, presidential candidates were allowed to spend up to 5bn naira (£2.8m; $3.7m) on campaigns ahead of the 2023 elections. That spending limit has since been doubled.

The cost of nomination forms alone puts the presidency beyond the reach of most aspiring young Nigerians.

The ruling All Progressive Congress (APC), along with the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and the African Democratic Congress (ADC) have each set their presidential nomination fee at 100m naira ($74,000; £56,000), making it extremely hard for new challengers to emerge.

Since the return to democracy in 1999, only two parties have governed Nigeria - the PDP from 1999 to 2015 and the APC since 2015.

These parties, alongside the ADC, formed last year by politicians who had defected from the other two, have established nationwide network of branches, supporters and campaigners.

Those aspiring candidates without the financial resources to secure nomination forms and compete in the internal party contests of the main parties have little chances of becoming president.

The barriers are also evident in the National Assembly.

Not one of Nigeria's 109 senators is under 40, while only 14 of the 360 members of the House of Representatives fall into that age group.

"I have been in politics for many years and I will tell you that young people in this country lack the resources to become president," says Dalhatu, who is running under Obi's Nigeria Democratic Congress.

Fatima Zahra Umar, a young politician in the APC who has previously tried to run for a seat in the House of Representatives, agrees.

"Young Nigerians are poor. Nigerian politics is cash-intensive, so participation is guided by money," she says, adding that young people are often content with having a bit of influence as a special advisor to a senior politician.

But political analyst Seun Ajayi believes the problems go beyond the financial barriers.

"We have some of the most brilliant young persons in the world, but they are either not interested in politics or feel satisfied when given a small role in government," he says.

"The old men are not going to sit idle and allow us to push them out. We have to fight for the big positions, but at the moment I don't see the zeal."

Umar believes changing attitudes towards young leadership is equally important.

"Culturally, we are not primed to trust or accept the brilliance of a younger person, so it will be very difficult," she says.

"Old men are still holding on to the system."

Some Nigerians took inspiration from the wave of success of young candidates in the recent midterm elections in the US, some of whom have roots in Africa.

"America Has Done It, Can Nigerians Do the Same?" entertainer Charly Boy wrote on X, in a post that was widely shared.

He said the US results served as a warning to Nigerian politicians that no matter how powerful the political machine, voters can change the direction of government.

He called on young people to interrogate candidates about their past promises: "Has life improved? Where are the jobs, security and affordable living?

"Democracy is not a spectator sport, nor is it about sharing rice," he wrote.

articles.title: Morte Gianni De Gennaro, la politica sotto choc: il cordoglio di Mattarella e Meloni
articles.summary: AGI - Servitore dello Stato, uomo delle istituzioni, figura di primo piano degli apparati di sicurezza. La politica è scossa dalla morte di Gianni De Gennaro, l'ex capo della Polizia che aveva collaborato con il giudice Giovanni Falcone ed era finito nell'inchiesta di Caltanissetta sul depistaggio delle indagini sulla strage di via D'Amelio, nella quale persero la vita il giudice Paolo Borsellino e gli agenti della sua scorta. Il corpo è stato ritrovato nella sua casa di campagna in provincia di Grosseto. I familiari non avevano sue notizie da ore e non riuscivano a raggiungerlo. Quindi l'allarme e la scoperta della morte. Secondo quanto riferito, si sarebbe trattato di un suicidio. Il cordoglio di Mattarella e Meloni Il presidente della Repubblica ha chiamato il comandante generale della Guardia di Finanza, Andrea De Gennaro, fratello di Gianni De Gennaro, per esprimere il proprio cordoglio in forma riservata. Anche la presidente del Consiglio, Giorgia Meloni, si rivolge ad Andrea De Gennaro e a tutti i familiari, dicendosi "profondamente scioccata dalla tragica scomparsa". E così il sottosegretario alla Presidenza del Consiglio, Alfredo Mantovano: "Sono sconvolto per la tragica morte di un servitore dello Stato, con il quale ho avuto modo di collaborare per anni e di cui ho ammirato le doti, il senso delle istituzioni e la dedizione al dovere". Il ministro dell'Interno, Matteo Piantedosi, ne ricorda "la serietà, la competenza e la dedizione", sottolineando come la scomparsa di "un grande funzionario dello Stato sconvolge e lascia sgomenti". La Russa e Fontana: prudenza nei giudizi e rispetto della dignità La morte di De Gennaro riapre il dibattito sulla riservatezza delle indagini e sulla prudenza nei giudizi. "Fino a quando non c'è un giudizio definitivo nessuno è condannato, credo che anche in questa tristissima vicenda ci sia modo di riflettere", dice il presidente del Senato, Ignazio La Russa. Sulla stessa linea il presidente della Camera: "Una vicenda drammatica che richiama una riflessione sulla necessaria prudenza nei giudizi e sul rispetto della dignità di ogni persona", avverte Lorenzo Fontana. Salvini e Vannacci criticano i processi mediatici Contro quelli che definiscono processi mediatici intervengono il vicepremier Matteo Salvini e il leader di Futuro Nazionale, Roberto Vannacci. "Sono sconvolto per la notizia della morte di un leale servitore dello Stato come Gianni De Gennaro, vittima di un massacro mediatico-giudiziario che una persona e una carriera come la sua non meritavano", dice Salvini. "Un servitore dello Stato vittima di quei processi mediatici giocati fuori dalle aule dei tribunali e molto cari a una certa stampa faziosa", rincara Vannacci. Per La Russa, tuttavia, occorre un supplemento di riflessione prima di trarre conclusioni sulle ragioni che hanno portato Gianni De Gennaro alla morte. A chi gli chiede se il suicidio sia dovuto a un momento di fragilità, la seconda carica dello Stato risponde con un invito alla cautela: "Prima di dire che il suicidio è fragilità ci rifletterei". Anche il ministro della Difesa, Guido Crosetto, respinge l'idea di una fragilità di fondo: "Forse il suo è stato l'ultimo coraggioso atto di servizio: non poteva accettare che qualcuno sporcasse quella storia che non era solo sua, ma delle istituzioni che ha servito". articles.body:
Finland says Russian helicopter violated its airspace

November 21, 2026

Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

A Russian helicopter is suspected of violating Finnish airspace, the Nordic country's Ministry of Defense said Saturday.

The incident happened a few hours after a drone attack left a Russian cargo ship ablaze in the Gulf of Finland, the easternmost part of the Baltic Sea.

What do we know?

According to Finland's Defense Ministry, the incursion happened at 12:34 p.m. local time (10:34 UTC/GMT) off the town of Loviisa, on the southern coast.

"This alleged airspace violation may be linked to rescue or surveillance operations carried out by Finland following damage sustained by a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland," public broadcaster YLE cited Defense Minister Antti Hakkanen as saying.

The ministry added the helicopter could have penetrated up to 4.1 kilometers (2.5 miles) into Finnish territory.

What do we know about the cargo ship attack?

Earlier Saturday, Finland — one of NATO's newest members — said a Russian cargo ship heading for Russia's Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad caught fire after being struck by drones in the Gulf of Finland.

The Finnish military said the Sparta II was damaged west of Russia's Gogland island, about 40 kilometers (25 miles) from Finland's coast, and later drifted into Finnish territorial waters.

Finnish Border Guard Commander Ilja Iljin later told YLE that the vessel, which is known to have links to the Russian military, was struck by Ukrainian drones while in Russian waters.

"At the moment, there is no confirmed information about what cargo is on board, but it cannot be ruled out that there is military materiel on board," Iljin said.

The ship is on a US sanctions list, according to a search of the Open Sanctions website.

The Border Guard later said the crew of the Sparta II was evacuating into a life raft and rescue boat.

Orpo backs Ukraine against 'aggressor'

"The [Ukraine] war is spilling over into our neighbouring areas," wrote Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo on X.

Ukraine has the right to fight against the aggressor," he added.

The Finnish government has put temporary curbs on aviation and maritime traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland.

The Defense Ministry said Finland had informed its allies about the incident.

articles.body:
Week-long efforts to agree a negotiating mandate for a legally binding international treaty to control the use of autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections.

Despite an overwhelming majority of states at the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW) in Geneva wanting to agree a negotiating mandate leading to a legally binding treaty, the need for consensus forced the conference to adopt a much weaker option.

The mandate asked countries “to elaborate by consensus”, an instrument that may not carry any legal obligations.

Although Russia led the objections using obstructive stalling tactics, other military powers invested in AI warfare, such as the US, were reluctant to commit to a legally binding protocol protecting civilians from robot drones and other autonomous weapons.

Some argued that international humanitarian law was sufficient. More than 100 states had been pushing for a new law, saying the weapons raised entirely new challenges. European and Nato states, including Ukraine, China and Iran, expressed support or willingness for a new protocol.

The US said the need for human control over autonomous weapons had been discussed at the Apec summit in meetings between president Xi Jinping and Donald Trump this week, but the US was reluctant to agree a binding treaty.

South Korea, Japan, Turkey, the UK, France and Germany were among the defence tech powers exploring AI-enabled weapons who also expressed resistance to being bound by a new law, instead advocating for a nonbinding agreement.

The CCW is a UN forum that operates via consensus, meaning all 128 parties to the convention have to agree unanimously to pass a statement. The high threshold has resulted in the CCW failing to pass any new laws regulating weapons in the past 30 years and states seeking pathways elsewhere to pass treaties, such as the 2008 ban on cluster munitions.

The Future of Life Institute’s chair, Max Tegmark, said world leaders had failed to meet the moment this week. “Slaughterbots are already here,” he said. “Yet states have agreed it is sufficient to just talk about this for the 14th year.”

Diplomats inside the negotiations said Russia had been deliberately filibustering and not working in good faith, as opposed to the US delegates, who had been seeking a path to reach a consensus statement.

The exclusion of several nonmember countries from negotiations also prompted a rare protest in the chamber on the final day of the conference, with the Egyptian delegation shouting at the conference chair.

Israel and the US have also used AI-enabled targeting systems to conduct tens of thousands of strikes in Gaza and Iran, which have resulted in mass casualties. The Pentagon struck more than 1,000 targets in Iran on the first day of the war, and according to investigative media reports, the US military is aiming to carry out 1,000 AI-assisted targeting decisions per hour.

Critics said this outcome was a missed opportunity, noting that states had been discussing the issue of autonomous weapons, their dangers, and the need for international rules on how to restrict and regulate them for 13 years and large substantive parts of a treaty had already been settled upon.

One European diplomat said: “There was no political will to really regulate these weapons. No will commensurate to the urgency and need.”

A Human Rights Watch’s senior arms adviser, Bonnie Docherty, who had been directly involved in previously successful treaties banning cluster munitions and nuclear weapons, said autonomous weapons needed binding law. She noted that treaties could be negotiated within 15 months and dismissed the US’s proposal of five years to sort out a mandate.

A bloc of seven countries – Austria, Belgium, Brazil, Ireland, Mexico, New Zealand and Panama – had led the push for a binding treaty to be negotiated within one year.

On Wednesday Brazil’s delegate told the floor: “These are not weapons of the future being discussed here, these are already in use and being further developed. We are late in developing these norms and rules to regulate these lethal autonomous weapons systems.”

articles.title: New EU budget proposal aims at tax gobal tech giants
articles.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

France has already rejected the plan as inadequate. European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a new draft for the next EU budget. articles.body:
EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal

November 21, 2026

European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a new draft for the next EU budget.

Among other things, he is suggesting a tax on big tech firms to ease the contributions of member states, some of which strongly criticised earlier proposals.

The EU budget is theEuropean Union’s shared budget and it is used for things ranging from agricultural subsidies, infrastructure projects to border control and defence.

A first draft for the 2028 to 2034 budget was proposed by the EU Commission in 2025 but was criticised, especially by a group of northern European members including Germany who wanted the budget to be much smaller.

Following that criticism, the European Council President has now suggested a new draft, which is smaller by €204 billion.

But divisions among member states appear to remain, with France immediately coming out against Costa’s new draft, saying it was "deeply disappointing."

What’s the plan for the tech tax?

The proposal includes a string of new "revenue channels," explicitly intended to "to keep national contributions at a reasonable level," so that member state will have to contribute less than otherwise would be the case.

The biggest splash would likely come from a tax on companies with an annual turnover from digital activities of at least 50 million euros in the EU and 750 million euros worldwide.

Those firms would be subject to "an annual contribution corresponding to 3% of the annual net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services and user-generated data," according to Costa.

Aside from the tech tax, the "balanced basket of new own resources" also includes taxes on tobacco products and electronic waste.

What happens next?

Neither the EU Commission nor European Council President Costa will have the final word on the budget. Costa's plan will now be at the centre of hours of talks when EU leaders meet in Brussels next week.

"This is a realistic budget that addresses our new priorities while preserving our established policies," Costa wrote about his proposal. "I am confident that this proposal is a good basis for moving towards a final agreement."

But an initial reaction from France suggests that any final agreement might still be some way off.

The French presidency said the budget "falls well short of what is needed, particularly on the Common Agricultural Policy, notably to guarantee income support for farmers."

"As it stands, this proposal from the President of the European Council does not provide a basis for an agreement."

The EU was hoping to reach a general agreement on the budget by the end of 2026 with its formal adoption planned for 2027.

articles.body:
South Africa

Tributes have been pouring in for South Africa's first female deputy president, Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, who has died at the age of 71.

A statement from her family said she passed away on Friday following complications from a medical procedure she underwent about two weeks ago.

She served as South Africa's deputy president from 2005 to 2008, having previously worked as minerals and energy minister.

The former deputy VP also had stints as United Nations under-secretary-general and headed its agency for gender equality, UN Women, from 2013 to 2021.

She has been praised for her decades-long work on social justice as well as the rights of women.

"Our hearts are really, really sad and broken for having lost such a very dynamic woman leader in our country," President Cyril Ramaphosa said.

"She truly flew the flag of women, not only women of South Africa and Africa, but women of the world," he said.

In a statement on X, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres praised Mlambo-Ngcuka as a "lifelong champion of the rights & empowerment of women and girls".

She "believed that gender equality is not a favour to be granted, but a right to be claimed", he said.

UN Women also paid tribute, lauding her courage and leadership, saying she inspired people around the world.

UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed recalled Mlambo-Ngcuka’s interventions on behalf of women and girls in Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and Nigeria.

"She pushed the limits and I think that that's where we got a lot of the confidence to do the things that we do, following in her footsteps," she said.

South African parliamentary officials, unions, and political parties have all been among those expressing their condolences.
